evals.query: Our Node project is native ESM ("type": "module" in package.json, no Babel). service.js imports { query } from './db.js'. Write a Jest test for service.js that replaces query with a mock returning [] and tell me how to run it.
expected_behavior: Runs Jest with node --experimental-vm-modules (for example through NODE_OPTIONS)
Imports jest from @jest/globals (or uses import.meta.jest) instead of relying on the global jest object
Mocks the dependency with jest.unstable_mockModule and a required factory, not jest.mock
Imports service.js with a dynamic await import() after registering the mock, not with a static import at the top
Does not claim that a second jest.unstable_mockModule call on an already imported module overrides it

evals.query: I have a function retryFetch(url) that awaits fetch(url) and, on failure, waits 1000 ms with setTimeout before trying again, up to 3 tries. Write a Jest test that checks it makes 3 calls when fetch always rejects, without the test actually waiting 2 seconds.
expected_behavior: Uses jest.useFakeTimers() (modern fake timers)
Advances time with jest.advanceTimersByTimeAsync or jest.runAllTimersAsync so promise callbacks run between timers, not with the sync advanceTimersByTime alone
Restores real timers after the test (jest.useRealTimers in afterEach or equivalent)
Asserts the call count with toHaveBeenCalledTimes(3), not a removed alias

evals.query: We are on Jest 30.5 with TypeScript 5.4. In a test of loadProfiles(ids), the injected fetchUser mock must resolve {id: 1} when called with 1 and reject new Error('not found') when called with 2. The test must also set process.env.API_URL to 'http://localhost' and spy on console.error, and both must be undone automatically when the test ends. Write the test, typing the spy explicitly.
expected_behavior: Configures the mock per argument with fetchUser.whenCalledWith(1).mockResolvedValue(...) and fetchUser.whenCalledWith(2).mockRejectedValue(...), rather than branching inside mockImplementation
Replaces the environment with jest.replaceProperty(process, 'env', ...) rather than assigning process.env by hand
Restores the spy automatically, with using spy = jest.spyOn(console, 'error') or jest.restoreAllMocks / the restoreMocks option
Types the spy with jest.Spied (or jest.SpiedFunction), never with the removed jest.SpyInstance, not even as an alternative
